selection.reason: RC38 found one physically coupled counter to be sufficient only in a fault-free finite model and explicitly left actual sensors at n=0. The highest-value next step without hardware is to state exactly which coupling, freshness, retention, and failure-domain assumptions turn that witness into a certificate, and to derive the minimum redundancy under one arbitrary independent witness fault.

researchQuestion: Under which declared fault sets does an authenticated sensor bundle uniquely determine whether a physical event occurred zero, one, or two times, and what is the smallest counterexample when event coupling, claim freshness, retention, witness independence, or common-cause exclusion is removed?
factsAtSeal: RFC 9334 separates claim-value generation from evidence generation and warns that a freshly signed evidence object may contain values generated much earlier; nonces and epoch IDs narrow recentness but do not create event coupling.

RFC 9684 requires a fresh nonce for TPM evidence yet places the relationship between each TPM and the measured component outside its scope; a root of trust for reporting does not alone prove physical sensor coupling.
RFC 9711 defines signed claims and freshness mechanisms but leaves verifier interpretation to the application profile and policy.

OPC UA Safety 1.05 uses monitoring numbers, timeouts, provider IDs, and integrity checks to detect transport corruption, repetition, sequence, loss, delay, insertion, and masquerade; the physical semantics of SafetyData remain application-defined.

The March 2026 TPM 2.0 Library specification provides current roots-of-trust primitives; a TPM counter or quote attests TPM-held state and becomes physical-event evidence only through a separately justified measurement-to-event path.
NASA's 2025 common-cause analysis states that redundancy improves reliability under independent failures but cannot lower total failure probability below a shared common-cause contribution.
NRC NUREG/CR-7313, completed December 2025 and published June 2026, identifies common-cause failure modeling and robust DI&C reliability estimates as current unresolved assessment challenges.
NIST metrological policy requires an unbroken calibration chain with each calibration contributing uncertainty and explicitly states that traceability alone does not guarantee fitness for purpose.
No physical actuator, calibrated sensor, HIL device, independent power or clock domain, second physical host, or hardware fault injector is available in this workspace.

hypotheses.claim: A signature over a current nonce makes the enclosed physical measurement current enough to identify event count.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: If claim-generation time is not event-bound, the same current token and reported value will be compatible with multiple current event counts; binding both token and measurement to the current event epoch removes this collision only when the sensor is otherwise healthy.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The unbound-claim model has no event-count collision, or the event-and-epoch-bound fault-free model retains one.

hypotheses.claim: Two diverse scalar witnesses are sufficient to identify event count with at most one arbitrary independent witness fault.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: A report pair such as [0,1] is compatible with truth zero and the second witness faulty or truth one and the first witness faulty; three reports have a unique strict majority when at most one is arbitrary.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Two witnesses identify every event count under one arbitrary fault, or three witnesses retain a collision under the same bounded and independent fault set.

hypotheses.claim: A current counter remains exact physical-event evidence even when reset or rollover is within the fault model.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: Reported zero is compatible with true counts zero, one, and two if an event-coupled counter may reset after the event; excluding reset and recording rollover are required certificate premises.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The resettable current-counter model uniquely identifies event count.

hypotheses.claim: Adding finite redundant witnesses can identify event count even if a common-cause channel may overwrite every witness coherently.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: For every finite n, any two truths can yield the identical vector [v]^n under a shared overwrite; the only escape is excluding that channel with evidence or adding a witness outside its failure domain.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Any tested n from one through seven identifies count under the declared common-cause channel, or the symbolic same-vector construction fails.

hypotheses.claim: Actuator command acceptance is sufficient evidence that the corresponding physical transition completed.
hypotheses.separatingPrediction: Acceptance before the energy or motion boundary admits accepted=1 with event count zero and one; only an event-bound completion record can remove the pair.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The acceptance-before-action architecture contains one event count per observation class.

causalChain.inputAndAllowedAssumptions: Physical event definition, count domain {0,1,2}, authenticated claims, declared independent arbitrary-witness budget f, explicit exclusions for reset and common-cause faults.
causalChain.bottleneck: A verifier-visible value may be authentic yet stale, reset, generated before physical completion, or replicated across witnesses sharing one failure domain.
causalChain.bridgeLemma: When every healthy report is event-bound, current, retained, and witnesses have disjoint failure domains with at most f arbitrary faults, strict-majority identification is possible exactly when n is at least 2f+1 in the scalar exact-report model.
causalChain.independentAdjudicand: The set of admissible true event counts inside each verifier-visible observation class, recomputed by an independent Python implementation.
causalChain.finalCriterion: A certificate may state an exact event count only if every accepted observation class contains one truth and all coupling, freshness, retention, calibration, and failure-domain premises have independent artifacts.

criteria: C2 command acceptance before action collides
C3 one healthy event-bound witness identifies
C4 one witness does not tolerate one arbitrary fault
C5 two witnesses do not tolerate one arbitrary fault
C6 three witnesses tolerate one arbitrary independent fault
C7 a fresh token does not freshen an old claim value
C8 binding event and measurement epoch identifies under zero sensor faults
C10 the strict-majority threshold matches every grid cell
C11 common cause defeats every tested redundancy size
C12 the common-cause counterexample is symbolic in n
model.stopRule: Stop without a scientific verdict if JavaScript and independent Python differ on architecture world counts, observation counts, collision counts, any threshold-grid cell, or common-cause sweep result. Preserve the first outputs before any code amendment.

futurePhysicalQualification.gate: A physical claim requires three physical hosts, calibrated and sealed raw measurements, explicit failure-domain separation, every preregistered power-cut and partition row, and ledger-blind adjudication. The design artifacts themselves are not experimental evidence.

uncertaintyBudget.model: Finite scalar reports and exact event counts; no analogue threshold, drift process, adaptive adversary, probabilistic dependence, unbounded count, clock skew distribution, or actuator dynamics.
uncertaintyBudget.measurement: Physical false-positive, miss, latency, hysteresis, saturation, drift, calibration transfer, reset, rollover, and environmental sensitivity are all unmeasured at n=0.
uncertaintyBudget.independence: Different labels or sensor principles do not prove disjoint power, clock, processor, storage, firmware, calibration, maintenance, environmental, or attack domains.
uncertaintyBudget.freshness: A nonce bounds token production after a challenge; the model separately requires evidence that the claim value was generated from the relevant current physical event epoch.
uncertaintyBudget.externalValidity: The 2f+1 threshold is an adversarial identifiability bound for scalar exact reports, not a complete safety-integrity or reliability calculation.
uncertaintyBudget.extrapolation: Sweeping common cause to n=7 is a regression test; the general impossibility statement rests on an explicit same-vector construction for arbitrary finite n.

safetyEthicsEnvironment: The current cycle executes no actuator. Any future rig must use energy-limited motion, guarded travel, emergency stop, electrical isolation, permitted radio/network behavior, non-human test subjects, and disposal procedures for damaged components.
